Mostly poor imitation of Battlefield 2042, which already isn't exactly a masterpiece. 

Steamcharts claims concurrent players of up to 70,000 but in Warfare mode I am regularly placed into near empty lobbies which don't fill up, so clearly there is manipulation going on with the statistics.

Vehicles feel awful, some of the worst driving mechanics in any FPS. Tanks should not drive on roller skates. 

It's free and very playable, but totally soulless.

citations.review_text:
Delta Force has been a lot of fun so far. The gunplay feels solid, the gameplay is engaging, and I really like the amount of customization available. Being able to fine-tune weapons and gear gives you plenty of room to build things around your own playstyle.

My biggest complaint is the menus and overall layout. Some things feel more complicated to find or navigate than they need to be, and the interface could definitely use some cleanup and better organization.

Overall, the actual gameplay is strong, the guns feel good, and the customization adds a lot of depth. With some improvements to the menus and UI, it would be an even better experience.

I half ass recommend this game. Like borderline not recommend.

I had a craving (and still do) for a pvp looter shooter so I decided to check this game out. The graphics are ok, combat is ok and each operator has their own skills like drones, crouch sliding, jammers etc. Sometimes the lobbies take long to fill so you may have to switch between servers. There are some SWEATY mfs so sometimes it's better to take low tier loadouts so you won't loose much especially in the beginning. 

There are some cheaters and spammers but when I reported I was notified pretty fast of the actions the gms took.

It is free so expect to see a few different currencies, tickets, coins and thingamabobs to earn to get skins and exp boosters. It can be overwhelming trying to figure out wtf they each do.

It's an ok game and better with friends to communicate with. Randoms often won't res you and just watch you die so they can take your loot. If you're burnt out from your main game and want to try something new check it out one weekend.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering cheaters using wallhacks and aimbots in matches.

citations.review_text:
To be honest, I am not trying to formally complain about cheaters all the time. The amount of cheaters in this game though is absolutely absurd and everytime I seem to send a report, I never hear back wether that player was banned or not. I have come across some games where the cheating is so blantant and obvious that it does make you question wether or not the anti cheat system really works. Its a fun game and great idea with the operators ect. the graphics are great.. but the cheaters is really what kills the game. Out of 5 matches you can expect at least 2-3 to have cheaters in them. 

If I could recommend something for the devs, do something like "Prime" added to CS2. Sure, it doesn't stop all cheaters but at least it adds a bit of a reason not to cheat otherwise they have to pay again to play with said "Prime" members. its not the best solution, but it is something. 6.5/10 is my rating for the game only based on the cheaters alone. Some of the abilities are also quite OP compared to the starting operators offered, along with some guns absolutely being unbalanced. On MULTIPLE occasions I have seen getting shot maybe 3-4 bullets and being downed, while I shoot almost a full clip into someone and they still stand.

Oh, lets not forget the RIDICULOUS "market" prices. Things being posted or selling for 1 million credits (1300 Credits is 135$ CAD) is beyond absurd. It makes you feel like this is one money hungry company

Rampant cheaters, wall hacks and Aimbot users plague this game, the devs ban them and then they just make new accounts. this game isn't even fun anymore because cheaters ruin it for literally everyone. they need to start doing some serious hardware bans.

Delta Force is a free-to-play tactical first-person shooter that successfully blends large-scale Battlefield-style warfare with a high-stakes extraction shooter mode.

Pros
* Completely free-to-play model offers massive multiplayer experiences with zero upfront cost.
* Features a highly diverse selection of game modes, ranging from 32v32 large-scale Warfare to the tactical, high-stakes Operations extraction mode.
* Exceptionally deep weapon customization (Gunsmith) system that allows you to craft highly precise weapon builds and easily share them with the community.
* Provides highly clear, accessible in-game map information, minimizing tedious memorization by explicitly marking extraction points of interest, safes, and bounties.
* Excellent cross-progression mechanics that allow you to seamlessly manage your inventory, black site crafting, and stats across PC, console, and mobile versions.

Cons
* The overall weapon and vehicle meta is frequently dominated by a few severely overpowered setups, heavily punishing casual or newer players who lack optimized, maxed-out loadouts.
* Free-to-play nature brings persistent challenges with hackers and cheaters across both the extraction and large-scale warfare modes.
* Map design features frustrating layout choices, frequently forcing entire lobbies into massive, repetitive choke points dominated by endless explosive spam.
* The user interface is heavily cluttered and confusing, making menu navigation and controller looting highly tedious.
* Live-service framework pushes an overwhelming amount of monetization pop-ups and features over-the-top, non-military operator cosmetics that clash with the tactical setting.

While players highly praise the smooth core gunplay, impressive visual fidelity, and the fact that it serves as a great, accessible hybrid between Battlefield and Escape from Tarkov, the community frequently criticizes the game for persistent server desync, optimization stutters, and the developers' reliance on aggre…

claims.claim: Reviewers state that unlocking new weapons and operators requires high requirements or spending money.

citations.review_text: There are a few things I really like and dislike about this game. Firstly, gameplay by itself is actually very fun. It's fun when you get a bunch of kills in a row or headshots. But it's not fun when you deal with people using cheats or no-lifers. It's also not fun that the requirements to unlock new weapons and operators are extremely high, and that it's just better to pay like 15 bucks for premium currency to unlock them. It's fun but I wouldn't say it's the best game ever.

Too many gadgets and classes in my opinion. A lot of which require eons of time to unlock and/or spend hard cash for immediate gratification. People say the game is overrun with cheaters. Perhaps this is true? It's difficult to be sure. Most cheaters don't fly around in games anymore. They use subtle cheats to improve their chances without detection.

Warfare Review (from an Attack/Defense perspective)

Delta Force scratched the itch for massive battles that I used to get from Battlefield 3, 4, 1, and 5.

Unfortunately, over time — especially during the last season — the game has become more frustrating than enjoyable.

Main Issues

Matchmaking

I’m playing from Europe, so this may differ depending on region.

Some matches are filled mostly with bots disguised as real players, often leaving only 2–4 actual players per team while the remaining 26–28 are AI. These bots also don’t get replaced by real players over time.

If the lobby isn’t bot-filled, matches often start with only 10–15 players per side, which usually causes the first sector to be steamrolled before the lobby fills up a few minutes later.

This doesn’t seem tied to weekday or time, although after 23:00 CEST, bot lobbies become extremely common.

Operator Abilities

Every season adds more operators and abilities, which sounds good in theory but hurts gameplay in practice.

At this point, you are constantly being spotted, tracked through walls, stunned, damaged, or forced out of cover by gadgets and abilities. Battlefield-style games always had spotting tools and explosives, but the sheer amount of unavoidable utility now makes gameplay feel overwhelming rather than tactical.

Map Pool

Recently, several maps were moved into a free DLC that is not installed by default.

In practice, this means you mostly rotate between the same four maps:
Cracked, Trench Lines, Aftershock, and Akh Canal.

Unfortunately, many of the better maps are now rarely seen:
Threshold, Knife Edge, Ascension, Shafted, Trainwreck, Cyclone, Monument, and Fault.

Server / Hit Registration Performance

Servers occasionally suffer from lag spikes or general instability. Since the whole lobby experiences it at once, it appears to be server-side and often tied to map events.

Its a really really fun game especially when it is free we can not complain much!. But for me and the reason I am giving this a negative review is because of horrible maps like Colosseum and Aftershock, I mean who even wants to play them !!! All I want is a map selector or at least a server browser or I don't think there is a point playing horrible maps they come up with every new season!

Feedback: Issues with Map Rotation, Weapon Balance, and Operation Mode
"I’d like to share some feedback regarding the current state of the game on the Steam platform:

Map Rotation: In Warfare mode, there are 12 maps available, but the rotation is stuck on only 4. This becomes repetitive very quickly.

Weapon Balancing: The bow is currently a one-shot kill, while sniper rifles require a headshot to kill, which feels inconsistent and unbalanced.

Operation Mode Limitations:

Skill Gating: Players who are not highly skilled are forced to repeat the 'Easy' difficulty loop indefinitely.

Platform Disparity: On Steam, the Layali map cannot be played as a team, whereas it is possible on the Garena platform.

Lack of Purpose: Operation mode has lost its core looting experience. Instead of scavenging for weapons or attachments, it has turned into a pure deathmatch.

Questing & Progression: As a casual player, completing quests to level up in Black Site is extremely difficult. Instead of being able to loot for mission objectives, the map feels like a hunting ground.

Spawning & Map Design: I would like to see the maps integrated like Layali, with more diverse and randomized spawn points. Currently, players check websites to memorize spawn locations, which makes it impossible for new players to survive as they are immediately targeted by veterans.

This makes the game incredibly frustrating for newer or less skilled players. If the game continues in this direction, it feels like we are being forced to use hacks just to stay competitive, which ruins the experience for everyone. Please consider these balance and quality-of-life improvements.

This was by far the worst update the game has ever had. The Aftershock update was bad in terms of performance, but after this one you play the same loop of maps forever even if you have installed all of them: Trench Lines, Aftershock, and Akh Canal, and that's it. I don't know what Team Jade was thinking, but this was a horrible decision. Casual players don't even know they have to install all the other maps. As is right now, I wouldn't recommend the warfare mode, which is what I play mainly.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game requires massive storage space, exceeding 100 gigabytes.

citations.review_text: The "Resource Management" Options Can't not be found in Official Launcher of this steam version. So you Need a Massive storage space (nearly 180GB with the latest version) to play this game.

Extremely fun gameplay. Basically a free battlefield with massive battles and usable vehicles (tanks, helis, jets and more), even has destruction and levolution moments in some maps. Every weapon is solid and fun to use and completely free, operators too. Only cosmetics and operator skins are paid but there's still a lot of free unlockables. Only downside I've seen is Warfare mode have way too many bots and sometimes full of extreme sweats.

There's also the extraction shooter Operations mode but I haven't played that much. Finding matches in that mode can be really hard unless you play on the popular maps and almost unplayable with randoms.

Biggest downside and annoyance is the optimization of this game. More than a hundred gigs just for multiplayer modes. And there's huge updates every once in a while. At least now there's the option of only downloading default or new maps but this game is still bloated asf. Along with insane lag and stuttering when joining a match or finishing it. 100+ fps during gameplay but still stutters like hell at times.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience performance issues including inconsistent framerates, frametime pacing problems, and random stutters during matches.

At least now there's the option of only downloading default or new maps but this game is still bloated asf. Along with insane lag and stuttering when joining a match or finishing it. 100+ fps during gameplay but still stutters like hell at times.

I really enjoy this game, but the engine behavior is really bad. Is anyone else having the same issue?

I'm getting:

* inconsistent FPS,
* bad frametime pacing,
* random stutters,
* and extremely high VRAM usage even on Low settings.

The worst part is when the "Aftershock" map appears. VRAM usage suddenly goes crazy and the game starts feeling much worse compared to other maps.

What confuses me is:
even on Low settings, VRAM usage is still extremely high, almost like changing graphics settings barely affects memory usage at all.

The game can feel amazing sometimes, especially the gunplay and overall gameplay, but the optimization and engine behavior completely ruin the experience for me.

I love this game, but at the same time I hate it because of these issues.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that solo players are at a severe disadvantage when matched against pre-made or stacked squads.

citations.review_text:
It keeps putting me into different servers when I just want to play on NA servers. It’s also a shame they don’t have a Solo Queue option where solo players can be matched against other solo players to make the game more balanced.

There’s a lot of great potential in this game, but there are still so many things that need to be adjusted and improved to make it a better overall experience.

The concurrent players on Steam charts are botted, most likely.

No SBMM despite the aforementioned "seemingly high playerbase", Warfare game mode (Battlefield-like) is 90% bots filling up the lobby, each team only has around 8 actual human players or less battling it out among bots in a 64-player server. So no wonder why it's fairly easy to rack up above 60 kills per game. It's the game where you just want to shot at anything that moves that barely shots back. 

TTK is ridicolously fast on Normal/Hard difficulty (Operations), practically requiring T5/Gold-tier equipment and ammo just to be competitive and it's the bare-minimum to have a chance, whereas easier modes like ZDE/Layali Grove feel far more balanced. It truly highlights just how poorly tuned their extraction game mode is. Some operators are broken than the others.

Fixed spawn points, you have to anticipate enemies from nearby spawn points within the first one minute of the raid, forced fights most of the time.

Playing solo is tough and straight up bad experiences, as you get matched up on Squad Fill with players who have their own objectives and no interest in teamwork/team composition, against pre-mades with try hard team comp every time. Game is just not solo friendly all around. 

No magazines to fill up with ammos. Magazine as far as weapon customization is concerned is only to increase the mag size. Therefore in this game it's the norm to put high tier ammunitions in your ass (secure container) rather than chest rig; you drag them out of your ass into your gun to reload. Ridiculous.

The playable boss 'Saeed' (and the guards) is overpowered and annoying to deal with sometimes depending on the kits, signifiicantly better than all the operators, at a cost. 

Sprint spam/run animation cancel (hold left Shift + W spam) to not make any footstep sound to push enemy behind a cover is the dumbest mechanic ever implemented in all shooter games I've played thus far.

Cheaters? of course, they exist. More lik…

If you are a solo gamer, this is not the game for you. You are put against stacked trios in every match. On top of that, its just dead for NA for Operation mode.

The devs need to limit normal mode gear to purple, and easy can be capped at blue. instantly dying to stacked trios with red/golden gear and ammo is not exciting, force them to go to hard mode with that gear.

I'll just sum this game up for you:
If you're solo, you're ♥♥♥♥♥♥ from the start. People will out util you every single time, you can't rat, as there is too many recon operators who will know your exact position just for existing as a solo. Once you're backed into a corner you'll be ♥♥♥♥♥♥ from both sides as they throw every single util into the room before killing you.

Easy mode - Either bot lobbies or it's filled with the sweatiest guys who just go to easy to kill noobs
Normal mode - Filled with fully kitted pvp sweats and the occasional cheater
Hard mode - Cheaters 99% of the time.

You wanna go squad fill? Get ready to have 0 communication, be sold and for people to not revive you if you get downed or die. Some people just squad fill to go solo. Others are just toxic and will steal your loot. Wish the game was in a better state for solo players but it's either rat as Noxx or die, you have no other option to doing bank in normal mode. 

I haven't had the luxury of playing with a normally kitted and communicated squad of friends, but if you do Im sure this game is much easier just because of the amount of util a team compared to a solo can have. Also Luna is op, and it won't change in a long time. Save your time, game's not worth it

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the anti-cheat system is ineffective and that matches contain players using aimbots and wallhacks.

citations.review_text: Way too many cheaters. It completely ruins the game and makes it frustrating to play. The developers really need to improve the anti-cheat system.

⭐⭐☆☆☆ 

Delta Force has potential, but the cheating problem seriously hurts the experience. The gunplay is fun and the large-scale battles can be exciting, but it's hard to enjoy the game when suspicious players seem to show up so often. Getting eliminated by obvious wallhacks or aimbots quickly turns what should be a competitive match into a frustrating one.

The core gameplay is solid, but until the anti-cheat situation improves, it's difficult to fully recommend. A good shooter buried under too many questionable encounters. 😕
